High values on the map are not always high mortality: small regions swing widely, and good reporters can look worse (#mortality-mapping)

sections.heading: Reports
sections.text:
The Reports page in the Output section builds reports from the loaded dataset. There are two kinds:

Kind | What it is | Files you can download
Document | Pages of text, charts and tables, with an optional cover page and contents | Word (

.docx

) or PDF
Slide deck | Slides with text boxes, charts, tables and pictures | PowerPoint (

.pptx

) or PDF

Charts and tables are drawn from the data every time you preview or download, so a report always reflects the current state of your analysis (years removed, adjustment, denominators). Every report you create is saved in the dataset and listed under Your reports. For downloading single charts and tables, datasets and the AI assistant, see Exports, reports and AI.

Reports are stored inside the dataset file. Creating or editing a report rewrites the saved dataset (the .rds cache), and the report list travels with it. Keep a copy of the dataset before you experiment, and share the dataset if you want a colleague to open your reports.

The page subtitle in the app still says "Word and PDF reports". The code also builds slide decks, and the one-pager is a PowerPoint deck.

sections.heading: Standard reports in the RMNCAH App
sections.text:
A standard report is the Countdown report of one analysis section, rebuilt as editable blocks. It opens as your own copy: change or delete anything. Text blocks written as questions (headed Notes or Interpretations) are prompts for the analyst; replace them with the interpretation agreed at your review meeting.

Standard report | Kind | What it contains | Page with a

Generate Report

button
Data quality | Document | Data quality summary table, district reporting rates, ANC1/Penta1 and Penta1/Penta3 consistency, with questions on score, completeness and outliers | Overall Data Quality Score
Data adjustment | Document | Background, then reported numbers before and after adjustment for institutional live births and Penta1, with a prompt to describe the effect in the latest year | Data Adjustment Changes
Denominator selection | Document | DHIS2 and UN projections of population, live births and under 1, then coverage of Penta3 and institutional live births under each denominator, national and by region | Denominator Selection
National coverage | Document | Coverage of ANC4, ANC in the first trimester, delivery care (institutional deliveries and institutional live births), PNC 48h, low birth weight, Penta3 and Measles 1; maternal and child continuum of care; family planning (FPET); districts reaching targets; continuum by region | Continuum of Care
National inequality | Document | For institutional live births and Penta3: coverage by region over time, map, equity by wealth and education; then coverage by district | Equity Assessment
Mortality | Document | Institutional maternal (iMMR), stillbirth (iSBR) and neonatal mortality trends, stillbirths per maternal death, completeness of death reporting | Mortality Completeness
Curative health services | Document | Service utilization data quality table, outpatient and inpatient charts and maps, preventive vs curative index | MCH Preventive vs Curative Index
Health system performance | Document | Health system inputs table and by-region charts (facilities, hospitals, health workers, beds), service outputs by inputs | PHC Performance
Public/private share | Document | Ownership of facilities and the private share of services, nationally and by rural/urban area | Public/Private Share
Synthesis chartbook | Document, chartbook page (13.9 x 22 in) | All six analysis areas (data quality and denominators, coverage and targets, equity and geography, mortality, curative services, health system) with interpretation questions and a cover for the country team | Reports page only
Sub-national one-pager | Slide deck, one 16:9 slide | One region: Penta3, institutional live births and ANC4 against other regions and over time, the data quality score table and a coverage table by district | Reports page only

Two of these are the ones most stakeholders ask for. The synthesis chartbook is the complete analysis in one document for the review meeting. The one-pager gives each region its own statistical profile.

sections.heading: Finish the prerequisites
sections.text: Reports stays locked until you have loaded a dataset and run Data Adjustment (see Data preparation). Choose denominators on Denominator Selection first: most charts use them.

sections.heading: Open it
sections.text: Click Reports under Output, or click Reports in the top header. A Generate Report button in a page header also opens the page and starts the matching standard report.

sections.heading: Choose a report
sections.text: Under Standard reports (documents) or Standard slide decks, click a card. Each card shows how many charts and tables it holds. You can also start from New document or New slide deck (Start blank).

sections.heading: Name it and choose its language
sections.text: A dialog asks for the report name (for example, the report and country), the Report language (English, French or Portuguese) and confirms with Create report. The report language is independent of the app language: the standard text is written in it, and the charts, tables and dates are always drawn in it. You can change it later on the Layout tab; charts and tables are redrawn, but text you wrote yourself is not translated.

sections.heading: Wait for the charts
sections.text: The editor opens at once. Each chart shows Drawing from the dataset and appears one by one. A chart that cannot be drawn shows Could not be drawn with this dataset with the reason.

sections.heading: Set the region, if the report has one
sections.text: For the one-pager (and any chart drawn for one region), pick the region on the Layout tab, under Report, in Region of this report. The first region in alphabetical order is chosen for you. Leave it empty for a national report. To produce a one-pager per region, duplicate the report from the list and change the region.

sections.heading: Edit, then check
sections.text: Replace the prompts, delete what you do not need, then open Print layout to see the final pages (see below).

sections.heading: Download
sections.text: Choose Download, pick the format and wait for the progress bar (Drawing charts from the dataset, then Writing the Word file, Printing the PDF or Writing the PowerPoint file). The file downloads by itself; Download again is offered if it does not.

sections.heading: The document editor
sections.text:
- Blocks panel (left). The Blocks tab lists every chart and table kind grouped by analysis area, with a search box (Search charts, tables, text); Text and layout holds Heading, Sub-heading, Paragraph, Notes box and Page break. Drag a block onto a page, or press + to add it after the selected block. The Outline tab lists the report's structure. A Custom group is announced for charts made for your dataset; it is empty for now.
- Chart and table settings. Select a block to set what it shows: Indicator, Level (National, Region or District), a variant such as Maternal or Child, Year, Region, Width (Full width, Half or Third), a title and Show caption and source. Customize this chart changes text, fonts and colours for this chart in this report only. Charts you customised in the app with Apply to: Report keep that styling.
- Order and removal. Drag a block by its handle, or use Move up, Move down, Duplicate and Delete. Undo and Redo (Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y) cover edits. Changes save automatically (Saved in the dataset).
- Text. Type directly. Enter starts a paragraph, Shift+Enter a new line. Insert Fields such as {country}, {region}, {first_year}, {latest_year}, {chart_indicator} or coverage values like {penta3_latest}; they are filled in from the data and follow the report language.
- Design. The Design tab holds themes (Countdown, Ministry of Health, Minimal, Formal), colours, fonts, the Cover page (title, subtitle, logos, country flag, editors, date, reference) and Contents. Layout sets page size (A4, Letter, chartbook, poster), orientation, margins, page numbers, header and footer. Browse for Themes builds a theme from a PowerPoint or Word file (.potx, .pptx, .dotx, .docx); downloads are then written from that file.
- Views. Edit, Read mode, Print layout (the exact final pages), Focus and zoom.
- Slide decks use a slide editor with layouts, a slide sorter, speaker notes and text boxes; charts and tables are placed on slides in the same way.

sections.heading: Formats and downloads
sections.text:
Format | Made by | Notes
Word

.docx | The app | Editable. On Windows with Word installed, Word also fills in the contents page and embeds fonts
PDF of a document | Made from the Word file by Microsoft Word or LibreOffice, so pages match Word exactly | If neither is installed, Chrome, Edge or Chromium prints it: close to the Word file, but pages can differ
PowerPoint

.pptx | The app | Text, charts and tables stay editable in PowerPoint
PDF of a slide deck | PowerPoint or LibreOffice | Not possible without one of them

The file is named after the country, the report name and the date, for example Kenya_Synthesis_chartbook_2026-09-26.docx, and is saved wherever your browser or DataSuite saves downloads. A document cannot be exported as PowerPoint, nor a deck as Word.

sections.heading: Prerequisites that change report content
sections.text:
- Removed years and adjustment decide the numbers in every coverage, adjustment and mortality chart.
- Denominators chosen on Denominator Selection are used by the coverage charts. Without them, the coverage-by-denominator trend chart says Choose the denominators first.
- Surveys. Equity charts and facility-versus-survey comparisons need the survey files you loaded.
- Country reference data. The FPET chart needs family planning estimates for the country.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.text:
Symptom | Likely cause and fix
Could not be drawn with this dataset

in a block | The dataset lacks the data. Read the reason after it, load the missing file or delete the block. The same text appears in the exported file
Choose a region | A regional chart has no region: set

Region of this report
No district coverage for ... in ... | Pick a year and region that have data
Final pages or PDF fail, or say a converter is missing | Install Microsoft Word or LibreOffice on the computer running the app. Word download still works
Slide deck PDF fails | Needs PowerPoint or LibreOffice. Download PowerPoint instead
Slow generation | The first draw of a long report, such as the synthesis chartbook, computes every chart. Wait for the progress bar; later edits redraw only what changed

sections.heading: Tips for stakeholders
sections.text:
- Settle data quality, adjustment and denominators before you generate the synthesis, and state them in a text block on the first page.
- Answer every interpretation prompt or delete it. Leaving prompts in is the most common reason a chartbook looks unfinished.
- Fill in the cover: title, editors, date and logos of the partners.
- Produce the report in the language of the audience, and use Print layout before you send a PDF.
- Duplicate the one-pager for each region and share the PowerPoint files with the regional teams.
- Link findings to actions: see Dissemination, decisions and action.

sections.heading: What this page does not cover
sections.text: Page notes added with the Notes button are not part of the report builder as far as the source shows. The Custom chart group is a placeholder. Where DataSuite saves downloaded files depends on your browser or desktop settings, which the report code does not control.

ai.summary: The Reports page builds documents (Word or PDF) and slide decks (PowerPoint or PDF) from the loaded dataset, from the app's standard reports or a blank page. Charts and tables are redrawn from the data each time, and every report is saved in the dataset: creating or editing a report rewrites the saved .rds, so keep a copy before experimenting.
steps: Finish the prerequisites: load a dataset, run Data Adjustment and choose denominators (#finish-the-prerequisites)
Choose a standard report or a blank document or deck, name it and pick the Report language (#name-it-and-choose-its-language)
Set the region on the Layout tab if the report has one (#set-the-region-if-the-report-has-one)
Replace the prompts, check Print layout, then Download (#edit-then-check)
rules: Text blocks written as questions (Notes or Interpretations) are prompts for the analyst to replace with the agreed interpretation (#standard-reports-in-the-rmncah-app)

PDF of a document needs Word or LibreOffice (else a browser prints it); PDF of a deck needs PowerPoint or LibreOffice; a document cannot be exported as PowerPoint, nor a deck as Word (#formats-and-downloads)
Removed years, adjustment, denominators and survey files change report content (#prerequisites-that-change-report-content)
Dissemination is covered in Dissemination (/en/docs/framework/12-dissemination/)
notCovered: Page notes from the Notes button; the Custom chart group is a placeholder; where downloads are saved (#what-this-page-does-not-cover)

sections.heading: Service utilization and health system
sections.text: Two groups in the Analysis section look beyond coverage of RMNCAH interventions. Service Utilization studies how much outpatient and inpatient care children receive. Health System Performance relates services to the inputs of the health system: facilities, beds, workforce and the private sector. Both need Data Adjustment to have been run. Methods: Service utilization and Health system performance.

sections.heading: Service Utilization
sections.text: Suggested order: check the data first, then read national and sub-national use, then the combined index.

sections.heading: Service Utilization DQA
sections.text:
Purpose. Judge whether OPD and IPD data are good enough to interpret.

Filter. A region selector (Select All for national results).

The page shows one table, Data Quality Metrics, by year. Its rows are the percent of expected monthly facility reports, the districts meeting the reporting threshold you set on Reporting Rate, the percent of non-missing OPD and IPD monthly values, the districts with no missing OPD or IPD values, OPD values that are not extreme outliers, districts with no OPD extreme outliers, the ratio of OPD to IPD for children under 5, and the percent of OPD and IPD that concerns children under 5. Download Plot and Download Data are in the toolbar.

If completeness or missingness is poor, treat utilization trends with caution.

Service utilization DQA

sections.heading: National Utilization
sections.text:
Tabs: OPD Visits (visits per person per year, all ages and under 5), IPD Admissions, Under 5 (share of OPD visits and IPD admissions that are children under 5), Case Fatality Rate (under 5 and all ages) and Deaths (proportion of deaths that are under 5). A second card, with Select Years and a Palette (default Purples), maps OPD Map and IPD Map by region.

Fewer than one OPD visit per person per year generally indicates poor geographic or financial access. Case fatality in facilities is a proxy for the quality of clinical care.

OPD visits

sections.heading: Sub-National Utilization
sections.text:
Choose a region (or Select All) to see the same tabs for that area, plus a second card, Sub-National Utilization, with the tabs OPD Visits and IPD Admissions showing the distribution across Admin 1 regions: OPD per child under 5 per year and IPD admissions per 100 children under 5.

Sub-national distribution of OPD

sections.heading: MCH Preventive vs Curative Index
sections.text:
Each dot is an Admin 1 region. The horizontal axis is the MCH Preventive services index (antenatal, delivery, postnatal and immunization services per child under 5, weighted by importance) and the vertical axis the Curative service use index (OPD visits and IPD admissions per child under 5, with admissions counted ten times a visit). Median lines divide the plot into four quadrants: low or high preventive, and low or high curative. Generate Report opens the service utilization report.

Regions with low preventive and low curative use are the priority; high curative use with low preventive use may show that people reach facilities only when ill.

MCH preventive versus curative index

sections.heading: National Health System
sections.text:
A table of health system indicators for the latest year, with the columns Indicator, Value and Unit, in three sections: Health infrastructure (facility density per 10,000, share of facilities that are hospitals, hospital density per 100,000, inpatient bed density per 10,000), Health workforce (workforce density per 10,000 and the ratio of nurse-midwives per physician) and Role of private sector (share of private and of NGO facilities). Download the table or its image from the toolbar.

National health system

sections.heading: Sub-National Health System
sections.text:
Tabs: Health Facility Density, Hospital Density, Workforce Density and Bed Density. Bars show each region against the National average line. For facilities (2 per 10,000), beds (25 per 10,000) and workforce (44.5 per 10,000) a dashed Target benchmark is drawn and bars are coloured Meets benchmark or Below benchmark. Hospital density has no benchmark.

Health facility density by region

sections.heading: PHC Performance
sections.text:
Tabs: Health Facility Density and Workforce Density. Each scatter plot relates an input to a service index for the Admin 1 regions. Dashed median lines split the chart into quadrants, for example high density with a low service index. Unusual regions are labelled. This is a descriptive comparison, not proof of efficiency.

Health system by region

sections.heading: Public/Private Share
sections.text:
The top card shows the ownership of health facilities as percentages of Private, NGO and Public. Below it, tabs National and Urban/Rural show the public and private split nationally and by area of residence.

The chart title currently reads Ownership of health facilities, 2024 (DHIS2). Check that the year matches your data before quoting it.

Public and private share

sections.heading: Common pitfalls
sections.text:
- Reading utilization trends without checking Service Utilization DQA first.
- Comparing health system densities with different denominators or population years.
- Treating a benchmark as a target for every region. It is a reference, and context matters.
- Interpreting a quadrant position as cause and effect.

ai.summary: Service Utilization studies outpatient and inpatient care for children; Health System Performance relates services to facilities, beds, workforce and the private sector. Both need Data Adjustment. Check the Service Utilization DQA before reading utilization trends.
rules: Fewer than one OPD visit per person per year generally indicates poor geographic or financial access (#national-utilization)
Benchmarks: facilities 2, beds 25 and workforce 44.5 per 10,000; hospital density has no benchmark (#sub-national-health-system)
A benchmark is a reference, not a target for every region; a quadrant position is not cause and effect (#common-pitfalls)
Methods are in Service utilization (/en/docs/framework/10-service-utilisation/)
Health system methods are in Health system performance (/en/docs/framework/11-health-system-performance/)
interpretation: Service Utilization DQA: one Data Quality Metrics table by year for OPD and IPD; poor completeness or missingness means caution (#service-utilization-dqa)
National Utilization: tabs OPD Visits, IPD Admissions, Under 5, Case Fatality Rate and Deaths, with OPD and IPD maps (#national-utilization)
MCH Preventive vs Curative Index: regions in four quadrants; low preventive and low curative use are the priority (#mch-preventive-vs-curative-index)
Sub-National Health System: region bars against the national average, with Meets or Below benchmark (#sub-national-health-system)
PHC Performance: inputs against a service index by region, a descriptive comparison, not proof of efficiency (#phc-performance)

sections.heading: Sub-national analysis
sections.text:
National averages hide the regions and districts that are being left behind. The Sub-National Analysis group has three pages: Sub-National Coverage, Sub-National Inequality and Coverage Target. They use the same adjusted data and the same denominators as the national pages (see Denominators). The method is described in Subnational analysis.

Expect more noise at district level than at region level. Small numbers, patient movement between districts and reporting gaps all produce implausibly high or low values.

sections.heading: Sub-National Coverage
sections.text:
Purpose. Compare DHIS2 and survey coverage estimates for each region or district.

When to use it. After National Coverage, to find the areas behind the national figure.

sections.heading: Open Sub-National Coverage
sections.text: It is in the Sub-National Analysis group.

sections.heading: Set the geography
sections.text: Choose the Admin Level. With Admin 1 a region selector appears, and with Admin 2 a district selector, so that you can focus on one area.

sections.heading: Pick an indicator tab
sections.text: ANC 4 Visits, Institutional Live Births, Low Birth Weight, Pentavalent 3, Measles 1, FP Projection or Custom for any other indicator.

sections.heading: Read the chart
sections.text:
The title names the area, for example the coverage estimates of the selected region. Lines show the DHIS2 estimate and the survey estimate, and the caption names the denominator used. Download Plot and Download Data are in the toolbar.

Sub-national coverage

How to interpret. Compare the region with the national line. A survey point far from the DHIS2 line in one region often signals a denominator or reporting problem there. Check the Reporting Rate of the region before drawing conclusions.

sections.heading: Sub-National Inequality
sections.text:
Purpose. Show how far each region (or each district inside a region) is from the national or regional figure, year by year.

Filters. Admin Level and, at Admin 1, a region selector to zoom in on one region.

Tabs are ANC 4 Visits, Institutional Live Births, Low Birth Weight, Pentavalent 3, Measles 1 and Custom. Each dot is a sub-national unit (Coverage at subnational unit) and the line is the national or, when a region is chosen, the regional coverage. A spread that narrows over the years means inequality is falling. The methodology summarises this spread with the median absolute deviation from the median (MADM).

Sub-national inequality

sections.heading: Coverage Target
sections.text:
Purpose. Show the percentage of districts in a region that meet a coverage target, by year.

Filter. A region selector. The level is fixed to districts.

Tabs are ANC 4 Visits, Institutional Live Births and Vaccine. The targets are the same as on the national page: at least 70% for ANC4, at least 80% for institutional live births and vaccines, and dropout below 10%. A table under the chart lists the districts that reach the target for the indicator chosen in its This table only control.

The goal is that all districts meet the target, so a higher percentage means less inequality.

Sub-national coverage against targets

sections.heading: Common pitfalls
sections.text:
- Reading a single district year in isolation. Look at the trend and the neighbouring years.
- Comparing regions that have very different populations without checking numerators.
- Forgetting that the denominator selected for the whole country also drives regional results. If one region looks impossible (above 100%), test another denominator before flagging the region.
- Ranking areas on the latest year only. Combine level, change over time, reporting completeness and denominator quality, as the methodology suggests.

ai.summary: Three Sub-National Analysis pages: Sub-National Coverage, Sub-National Inequality and Coverage Target. They use the same adjusted data and denominators as the national pages. Expect more noise at district level than at region level.
rules: Targets are the same as nationally: ANC4 at least 70%, institutional live births and vaccines at least 80%, dropout below 10% (#coverage-target)
Check the region's Reporting Rate before drawing conclusions (#read-the-chart)
Do not read a single district year in isolation; if a region looks impossible (above 100%), test another denominator before flagging it (#common-pitfalls)
Rank areas on level, change over time, reporting completeness and denominator quality, not the latest year only (#common-pitfalls)
The method is in Subnational analysis (/en/docs/framework/7-subnational-analysis/)
interpretation: Sub-National Coverage: DHIS2 and survey lines for the chosen area; compare with the national line; a survey point far from DHIS2 in one region often signals a denominator or reporting problem there (#read-the-chart)

Sub-National Inequality: dots are sub-national units, the line is national or regional coverage; a spread that narrows means inequality is falling; the methodology summarises it with MADM (#sub-national-inequality)
Coverage Target: percentage of districts in a region meeting the target; the goal is that all districts meet it (#coverage-target)

sections.heading: Coverage, equity and targets
sections.text: The National Analysis section has four pages: National Coverage, Coverage Target, and under National Inequality the pages Routine Data (inequality between regions) and Survey Data (the Equity Assessment). All of them use the vaccination denominator you chose in Denominators, and all need adjusted data. Sub-national versions are in Sub-national analysis. Methods: coverage and equity.

sections.heading: Indicators available
sections.text:
Each page shows a strip of tabs, one indicator per tab. Most tab strips end with a Custom Check tab that opens an Indicator selector listing every Vaxx analysis indicator:

- ANC 1, Institutional Deliveries and Institutional Live Births.
- BCG, IPV 1 and 2, Measles 1 and 2, OPV 1 to 3, Pentavalent 1 to 3, PCV 1 to 3, Rotavirus 1 and 2.
- Dropout: Penta 1 to Penta 3, Penta 1 to Measles 1, Penta 3 to Measles 1, Measles 1 to Measles 2. Dropout is the number of children who received the first dose minus those who received the second, divided by the first, as a percentage.
- Zero-dose and Under-vaccinated, derived from Penta1 and Penta3.

sections.heading: National Coverage
sections.text: Compares DHIS2 and survey estimates of national coverage for each indicator.

sections.heading: Pick an indicator tab
sections.text: Choose a headline indicator, or Custom Check for any other.

sections.heading: Read the chart
sections.text: The chart is titled "National ... Coverage Estimates" and plots by year the DHIS2 estimate, the WUENIC estimate and the Survey estimate with its 95% CI. The caption states which denominator the DHIS2 values use.

sections.heading: Use the chart tools
sections.text:
Each chart has a toolbar to edit labels, change view or style, download the image and download the data. See Exports, reports and AI.

National coverage

Interpretation: DHIS2 lines that track the survey and WUENIC points support the chosen denominator. A persistent gap, or DHIS2 above 100 percent, points to a denominator or numerator problem. Return to data quality and denominators.

sections.heading: National Inequality: Routine Data
sections.text:
Shows how national coverage differs between regions, using facility data.

- Tabs and the Custom Check tab as above. Each chart shows coverage in every Admin 1 region by year (subtitle "Subnational unit: admin 1 level") against the national line.
- Select Years and Palette (Greens, Blues, Reds, Purples) filters drive the Sub-National Mapping card, where each tab draws a map titled "Distribution of ... by Regions" from DHIS2 data. The map follows the tab selected in the inequality card.

Wide spread between regions means the national average hides weak areas. Investigate them in Sub-national analysis.

National inequality

sections.heading: National Inequality: Survey Data (Equity Assessment)
sections.text: Compares coverage across household groups from the survey files loaded in the wizard.

sections.heading: Choose the Equity Type
sections.text: Area (Rural, Urban), Maternal Education (No education, Primary, Secondary or higher) or Wealth Quintile.

sections.heading: Choose the indicator
sections.text: Tabs are Pentavalent 3, Measles 1, and the dropouts Penta 1 to Penta 3 and Penta 3 to Measles 1, plus Custom Check.

sections.heading: Read the equiplot
sections.text:
The chart is titled "Inequalities in ... coverage by ..." and shows coverage for each group. Distance between the points is the inequality.

If a survey file was not uploaded, the built-in reference data are used. Upload the country's files in the Load Data wizard for a real assessment.

sections.heading: Coverage Target
sections.text:
Tracks the share of sub-national units meeting global targets. On this page use Admin Level (Admin 1 or Admin 2). Two tabs:

Tab | Indicators | Unit meets the target when
Vaccine | BCG, Pentavalent 3, Measles 1 | Coverage is at least 80 percent in the region or district
Dropout | Penta 1 to Penta 3, Penta 3 to Measles 1 | Dropout is below 10 percent

The chart title states the threshold that was applied, and the bars show the percentage of units meeting it by year and indicator. The table below the chart (Target Rate by Region at Admin 1, Sub-National with coverage for Admin 2) lists the units that reach the vaccine threshold for the indicator and year chosen in its own selectors. It can be downloaded as an Excel file.

A rising percentage of units meeting the target is good news only if coverage does not exceed plausible levels. Check units far above 100 percent for denominator problems. For dropout, remember that lower is better, and read the chart title for the direction.

Coverage against targets

sections.heading: Pitfalls
sections.text:
- Coverage and target pages change when you change the denominator. Record which denominator a result used (the chart caption shows it).
- Equity charts come from survey files and can be several years old. Compare them with routine trends, not with a single year of DHIS2 data.
- Zero-dose and Under-vaccinated depend on the denominator even more than dose coverage does.

Next: Sub-national analysis.

Zero-dose and Under-vaccinated are derived from Penta1 and Penta3 (#indicators-available)

For dropout lower is better; check units far above 100 percent for denominator problems (#coverage-target)

sections.heading: Data preparation
sections.text:
Data preparation turns the reported data into the dataset used for coverage. It has three pages: Remove Years, Data Adjustment and Data Adjustment Changes. The rules are explained in the data adjustment chapter.

Adjusting the data is required. Denominators, coverage, inequality, targets and Reports stay unavailable until you run Adjust Data at least once.

sections.heading: Remove Years
sections.text: Use this page to leave out years whose data cannot be relied on, for example a year with almost no reporting or a known system failure.

sections.heading: Decide from the data quality pages
sections.text: Confirm with the data quality pages that a year is unusable.

sections.heading: Select the years
sections.text: In Select Years to Remove, choose one or more years.

sections.heading: Confirm
sections.text:
Choose Confirm Removal. The message box then reads "Data for the following years has been removed" and lists them. To restore years, clear the selection and confirm again ("No years have been removed yet").

Remove years

Removal happens before adjustment. If you have already adjusted, run Adjust Data again after changing the removed years.

sections.heading: Data Adjustment
sections.text:
The page has two cards.

K-Factors (Adjustment Factors): an ANC K-Factor, a Delivery K-Factor and a Vaccines K-Factor, each a choice of 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 or 1. The K-factor is the assumed service volume of non-reporting facilities relative to reporting ones. The framework default is 0.25, and the page shows the values stored in the dataset.

Adjust: Adjust Data applies the corrections to the current dataset. The adjustment covers missing reports and extreme outliers. The status box shows "Not adjusted yet", then "Adjusting ...", then "Data Adjusted". Once adjusted, Download Adjusted Dataset saves master_adj_dataset.dta.

sections.heading: Choose the K-factors
sections.text: Pick a value for each of the three factors. Keep 0.25 unless you have evidence that non-reporting facilities carry a different share of services, for example a large private sector that reports poorly.

sections.heading: Run the adjustment
sections.text: Choose Adjust Data and wait for "Data Adjusted".

sections.heading: Review the changes
sections.text:
Open Data Adjustment Changes.

K-factor selection

sections.heading: Data Adjustment Changes
sections.text:
Shows how the adjustment changed each indicator. Under Visualize effects of changes, tabs are Institutional Live Births, BCG, Pentavalent 1 and Measles 1, plus a Custom Check tab with an indicator selector. Each chart compares the number of the indicator before and after adjustment for completeness and outliers.

If the data have not been adjusted, the chart uses a K-factor of 0 for every service, so it shows only what outlier and missing value handling do.

Before and after adjustment

sections.heading: Interpretation and pitfalls
sections.text:
- Small differences between before and after are normal. A large jump in one year points to very low reporting or to an outlier that needs a second look in Outlier Detection.
- According to the framework, months or districts with reporting below 75 percent are not scaled up, so adjustment cannot repair very incomplete data. Consider removing such years.
- Changing K-factors, removed years or the performance threshold affects every downstream page. Re-run Adjust Data and re-check denominators afterwards.
- Reports and pooled caches should be built from adjusted data. See Pooled App.

Next: Denominators.

sections.heading: Data quality
sections.text: Data quality is the first analysis stage. Five pages under Data Quality Assessment show how complete, plausible and consistent the routine data are. Their results decide whether you remove years and how you adjust the data. Methods are described in the data quality assessment chapter.

sections.heading: When to use it
sections.text: Use these pages right after loading the data, and again whenever you upload a corrected file. Review them in this order: Reporting Rate, Outlier Detection, Data Missingness, Internal Consistency, Overall Data Quality Score.

sections.heading: Common filters
sections.text:
- Indicator: pick what to assess. Outlier, missingness and consistency pages list all Vaxx indicators (ANC1, Institutional Deliveries, Institutional Live Births, BCG, IPV 1-2, Measles 1-2, OPV 1-3, Pentavalent 1-3, PCV 1-3, Rotavirus 1-2). Reporting Rate uses three service groups: ANC, Institutional Delivery and Vaccination.
- Admin Level: Admin 1 (regions) or Admin 2 (districts). A region selector lets you focus on the districts of one region.
- Performance Threshold (Reporting Rate only): a percentage, 90 by default with quick picks of 70, 80, 90 and 95. It is saved in the dataset and reused by the Overall Data Quality Score.

sections.heading: Reporting Rate
sections.text: How completely facilities reported, by year and area.

sections.heading: Choose the service, threshold and admin level
sections.text: Select ANC, Institutional Delivery or Vaccination, set the threshold, then the admin level.

sections.heading: Read Sub-National Reporting Rate
sections.text: The Heat Map tab shows the reporting rate for each area and year. The Bar Graph tab shows the rate by year.

sections.heading: Read the National Reporting Rate card and the table
sections.text:
The National Reporting Rate card shows the percentage of districts with low reporting (below the threshold) by service and year. Sub-National Units with Low Reporting lists the areas below the threshold for the selected year and service.

Reporting rate by year

sections.heading: Outlier Detection
sections.text:
Finds extreme monthly values that may be data entry errors. A value is an outlier when it lies more than 5 median absolute deviations (MAD) from the median (Hampel method).

- Indicators with Outliers card: tabs Heat Map (percent of non-outlier values by area and year), Indicator Bar Graph (by year and indicator) and Region Bar Graph (by year and region).
- Sub-National Units with Extreme Outliers: table of year, month, area, reported value, median and MAD. Pick the year with the "This table only" control.
- Sub-National Trends: monthly plot for one region and the selected year, showing the reported value, the median, the outlier bounds (plus and minus 5 MAD) and the outliers.

Outlier detection

sections.heading: Data Missingness
sections.text:
Shows which indicators and areas have missing data.

- Tabs Heat Map (missingness percentage by area and year), Complete Indicators (percent of districts with complete data for the indicator) and Missing Indicators by Region (trend in completeness by region).
- Sub-National Units with Missing Data: table of areas with incomplete data for the selected indicator and year. The indicator selector has a Select All option.

Data missingness

sections.heading: Internal Consistency
sections.text:
Checks that related indicators agree over time.

- Ratio Plots: ratios ANC1 / Penta1, Penta1 / Penta3 and OPV1 / OPV3 by year, compared with the expected ratios.
- Consistency Checks: tabs ANC1 and Penta1, Penta1 and Penta3, OPV1 and OPV3, IPV1 and IPV2, and Custom Check where you choose the X and Y indicators. Each plot draws one point per district and year, with a linear fit and a diagonal. Points far from the diagonal indicate inconsistent reporting.

Consistency checks

sections.heading: Overall Data Quality Score
sections.text:
One annual score across all checks. Filter by region or use the national level. The table has three blocks:

- Completeness of monthly facility reporting (mean of ANC, delivery, immunization): percent of expected monthly reports nationally, and percent of districts with completeness at or above the threshold, and percent of districts with no missing values (mean for common vaccines).
- Extreme outliers: percent of monthly values that are not extreme outliers, and percent of districts with no extreme outliers in the year.
- Consistency of annual reporting: the three ratios and the percent of districts with ANC1/Penta1, Penta1/Penta3 and OPV1/OPV3 in the expected range.

The last row is the Annual data quality score. Use the two download buttons on the card to save the plot and the data.

Overall data quality score

sections.heading: Interpretation and pitfalls
sections.text:
A high national reporting rate can hide many low-reporting districts. Always check the district view and the score by region.

- A year with many outliers or low completeness is a candidate for Remove Years or careful adjustment.
- Consistency plots show plausibility, not truth: an unusual Penta1/Penta3 ratio can be a real dropout problem or a data problem.
- Changing the threshold changes the score, so agree it with your team before comparing years or countries.

Next: Data preparation.

Review them after loading, in order: Reporting Rate, Outlier Detection, Data Missingness, Internal Consistency, Overall Data Quality Score.

sections.heading: Denominators
sections.text: Coverage is a number of vaccinated children divided by a target population, so the choice of denominator matters as much as the data quality. This section has two pages under Denominators: Population Trend (the Denominator Assessment page) and Denominator Selection. Both need adjusted data. The method is in the denominator selection chapter.

sections.heading: When to use it
sections.text: Use these pages after adjustment and before reading any coverage result. Repeat them if you change the adjustment or the survey inputs.

sections.heading: Population Trend
sections.text:
Compares population trends across the available sources.

- Filter Select Best Population: Live births (DHIS2), Total births (DHIS2), Total population (DHIS2) or Under 1 year (DHIS2). It sets the DHIS2 population the derived denominators are built from.
- Card Population Comparison with tabs Population, Births and Under 1. Each chart plots the UN projection against the DHIS2 projection by year (in thousands).

Look for a stable, plausible gap between UN and DHIS2. A sudden break in one line usually means a change in how the population was projected, not a real change in births.

Population trend

sections.heading: Denominator Selection
sections.text: Compares coverage under each denominator option and records your choice.

sections.heading: Read the survey comparison
sections.text:
The National Coverage card has tabs Institutional Live Births, BCG, Pentavalent 3 and Measles 1. Each chart shows the facility-based coverage from DHIS2 under each denominator, next to the national survey coverage for the survey year. A denominator that gives coverage close to the survey, without exceeding 100 percent, is a good candidate.

If survey estimates are missing, the card shows "No coverage to show yet" and a Go to Load Data button. Add the survey values in the National Rates step.

sections.heading: Check the regional pattern
sections.text: Subnational Derived Coverage has tabs Pentavalent 1, Pentavalent 3 and Measles 1. It compares regional estimates by denominator for the survey year.

sections.heading: Check the trend
sections.text: Population Trend (on this page it means coverage over time) has tabs Pentavalent 1, Pentavalent 3 and Measles 1. Each shows coverage by year under every denominator, including the UN population. Use the Admin Level filter (National, Admin 1, Admin 2) and the region selector to look at one area.

sections.heading: Choose the denominator
sections.text:
Set the Vaccination denominator chip. Options are DHIS2, ANC 1, Pentavalent 1, Penta1-derived and ANC 1 Population Growth. The choice is saved in the dataset and used by every coverage, inequality and target page. The Vaxx App has one vaccination denominator, with no separate maternal one.

Best denominator selection

National coverage over time by denominator

sections.heading: What each option means
sections.text:
Option | Idea
DHIS2 | The population projected in the DHIS2 data (live births, total births, total population or under 1, per the Select Best Population setting).
ANC 1 | Denominator derived from ANC-1 service utilization.
Pentavalent 1 | Denominator derived from Penta-1 immunization.
ANC 1 Population Growth, Penta1-derived | The ANC-1 or Penta-1 derivation with an adjustment for annual population growth.

The UN projection is also plotted on the charts for comparison, but it is not one of the choices in the chip.

Definitions of derived populations and survey rates are in the framework chapter.

sections.heading: Interpretation and pitfalls
sections.text:
A denominator derived from Penta1 makes Penta1 coverage look near 100 percent by construction. Judge it on Penta3 and Measles 1, and against the survey.

- Do not pick the option that gives the highest coverage. Pick the one that best agrees with the survey and stays consistent over time.
- Sub-national denominators can be less reliable than national ones. Read them together with district data quality.
- The vaccination denominator label appears as a chip on every analysis page. If results look odd, check it first.

Next: Coverage, equity and targets.

sections.heading: Exports, reports and AI
sections.text: This page covers what you can take out of the Vaxx App (images, tables, datasets and reports) and how the DataSuite chat assistant can work with the same data. Dissemination planning is discussed in the dissemination chapter.

sections.heading: Charts and tables
sections.text:
Every chart has a toolbar in its card header:

Tool | What it does
Ask AI | Placeholder for a future feature ("coming soon").
View options | For this chart only: orientation (Auto or Swap axes), text size, legend position (Right, Bottom, Hidden).
Edit labels | Change the title, subtitle, caption, axis and legend titles of this chart. An empty field keeps the original text. Applies to the chart and its image download. Edited text is not translated.
Style options | Fonts, colours, angles, legend, axes, grid and background of this chart. Saved with the dataset.
Download Plot | Saves the chart as a PNG image.
Download Data | Saves the data behind the chart as an Excel file.
Expand chart | Enlarges the chart.

Tables have a Download Data button (Excel). Tables with a year or indicator selector filter only that table, as the hint "This table only" says. The Overall Data Quality Score card has one button for the plot and one for the data.

Downloads follow what you see: the current indicator, admin level, region and denominator. The file name carries the indicator and denominator, for example penta3_....

sections.text:

The wizard also saves the whole analysis as name_vaccine.rds (see Getting started). That file is the cache used by the AI tools below and by the Pooled App.

sections.heading: Reports
sections.text: The Reports page in the Output section builds documents (Word or PDF) and slide decks (PowerPoint or PDF) from the loaded dataset, starting from the standard reports of this app or from a blank page. It needs adjusted data. Charts and tables are redrawn from the data every time, and every report is saved in the dataset. The full guide, with each standard report, the editor, export formats and troubleshooting, is on the Reports page.

sections.heading: The DataSuite chat assistant
sections.text:
While Vaxx is the active app, the DataSuite chat agent can analyse the same data. This needs DataSuite 1.131 or later and R with the cd2030.core package available to DataSuite's managed R session. Two tools are provided:

Tool | What it does
Look Up cd2030.core Data Reference

(

cd2030Docs

) | Lists the app's pages, which

CacheConnection

methods and fields each page reads, their technical documentation and, where available, the rationale for why the numbers matter. It can also look up one method, for example

calculate_coverage

.
Read Countdown Cache

(

readCd2030Cache

) | Opens the app's

.rds

cache in the managed R session as

.datasuite_cache

. It always reloads from disk, so answers never come from stale data.

Chat instructions apply automatically. They tell the agent to look up the data reference before writing R code, load the cache with readCd2030Cache, prefer the methods of cd2030.core over re-deriving indicators, and record durable analysis decisions so that they are not silently re-decided later.

sections.heading: Save your work
sections.text: Finish the wizard so that the dataset is saved as an .rds cache, and adjust the data.

sections.heading: Ask a question
sections.text: For example: "Which districts have Penta1 to Penta3 dropout above 10 percent in the latest year?" or "Explain why the survey and DHIS2 Measles 1 coverage differ."

sections.heading: Check the answer
sections.text: The agent should name the methods it used. Compare its numbers with the app charts before quoting them, and see the AI chapter for good prompts.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.text:
- The data reference lists the 18 Vaxx analysis pages (upload, data quality, preparation, denominators, coverage, inequality, equity and targets). It does not describe the Introduction and Reports pages.
- Ask AI buttons in the chart toolbars are not active yet. Use the chat assistant instead.
- AI output must be checked by an analyst. See Leveraging AI for analysis and interpretation.

sections.heading: Open the app
sections.text:
Open DataSuite, go to the Start page and choose Vaxx. The app opens on the Introduction page, which presents the Countdown immunization coverage and inequalities project in English, French or Portuguese. Use Load Data in the left navigation to begin.

If you launch the app by opening a data file in DataSuite, that file is loaded for you.

sections.heading: Accepted files
sections.text:
Format | Notes
.xlsx

,

.xls | A workbook with an

Admin_data

sheet, a

Population_data

sheet, a

Reporting_completeness

sheet and at least one

Service_data

sheet. Starts the full walkthrough.
.dta | A single, already merged Stata file.
.rds | A dataset saved by this app. It is already validated, so the app opens a summary of the dataset instead of the walkthrough.

Files of up to 2 GB are accepted. Other extensions are refused with "Upload failed: Unsupported file format."

When you upload an Excel or Stata file, the app looks for a saved copy named name_vaccine.rds and loads it instead if it exists. This is how work resumes. In a desktop session the copy sits next to your file; from a browser it is kept in a fixed local folder.

sections.heading: The Load Data wizard
sections.text: The wizard has a step rail. Steps unlock in order, and a step marked required must be complete before the next one opens.

sections.heading: Upload Data
sections.text: Drop or browse for your file in the Dataset card ("Browse or Drop..."). Under Additional reference data (optional) you can upload your own UN estimates and WUENIC estimates to replace the built-in reference datasets. Download Master Dataset saves the merged data as master_dataset.dta. Clearing the file also clears everything derived from it.

sections.heading: Data Quality
sections.text:
Checks run automatically on the loaded sheets. Blocking checks must pass before you can continue:

- The Admin, Population and Service sheets are found.
- The country name is recognized, and the Admin sheet names exactly one country.
- The Admin sheet has country, admin-1 and district columns.
- Districts match between the Admin sheet and every other sheet, and district names are consistent across years.
- No month is missing for any district-year, and every month value is a recognized English or French month.

Informational checks do not block. They flag estimated live births below reported institutional counts, population figures that look pasted into service data, indicators with no data at all, and month names written differently across sheets. Two mapping checks report survey or shapefile region names that do not match your data.

sections.heading: Survey Files (optional)
sections.text: Upload the national, regional, area, maternal education and wealth quintile survey files (.dta), one at a time. Without them the app keeps its built-in reference data.

sections.heading: National Rates
sections.text: Confirm the survey coverage (percent, 0 to 100) for ANC1, institutional delivery, BCG, Penta1, Penta3, OPV1, OPV3 and Measles 1. Confirm the national rates (proportions, for example 0.03 for 3 percent, range 0 to 0.05) for pregnancy loss, twin births, stillbirth, neonatal mortality and post-neonatal mortality. Also confirm the Survey Data Start Year and Recent Survey Year. Values found in your national survey file are pre-filled, so check them. Every field is required.

sections.heading: Shapefile (optional)
sections.text: The standard shapefile for the country is used by default. To use your own, upload it and say which column holds the region (admin-1) names.

sections.heading: Map Survey and Map Shapefile
sections.text: When you uploaded survey files or a custom shapefile, match their region names to those in your dataset. Names are matched automatically where possible, but you must review and save the matches even if nothing needs correcting.

sections.heading: Finish Loading Data
sections.text: The dataset is saved and the wizard shows Ready for analysis, with a summary (rows loaded, checks passed, fields set, files uploaded, regions mapped). Choose Continue to analysis. Use Edit on the summary to return to any step.

sections.heading: Vaxx App overview
sections.text:
The Vaxx App is the DataSuite app for immunization coverage and inequalities. It takes a country's routine facility data (usually exported with the Data Extractor), checks and adjusts it, chooses a denominator, and then estimates coverage for routine vaccines, dropout, zero-dose and under-vaccinated children. Coverage can be compared with survey and WUENIC estimates, followed over time, split by region, district, area of residence, maternal education and wealth, and tracked against global targets.

It follows the same CD2030 analytical framework as the RMNCAH App, but is narrowed to immunization: the indicator list, the survey inputs, the adjustment factors and the analysis pages are all immunization-specific.

sections.heading: Who it is for
sections.text:
- Immunization programme managers and national EPI analysts who need routine coverage estimates that are quality-checked and comparable with surveys.
- Analysts in the Countdown immunization coverage and inequalities work, at national and district level.
- Anyone who needs a Word, PDF or PowerPoint report of data quality and coverage for a country.

Input | Details
Facility data | One file per country:

.xls

,

.xlsx

,

or

Admin_data

sheet, a

Population_data

.

Survey files (optional) | National, regional, area, maternal education and wealth quintile

.dta

files, needed for the Equity Assessment and survey comparisons.

DataSuite | The app runs inside DataSuite. Open it from the Start page.

sections.heading: How Vaxx differs from the RMNCAH App
sections.text:
| Vaxx App | RMNCAH App
Focus | Immunization | Reproductive, maternal, newborn, child and adolescent health
Indicators | ANC1, institutional deliveries and live births, BCG, IPV 1-2, Measles 1-2, OPV 1-3, Pentavalent 1-3, PCV 1-3, Rotavirus 1-2, plus derived dropout, zero-dose and under-vaccinated indicators | ANC (including ANC4, IPT, syphilis, IFA, HIV test), delivery, C-section, low birth weight, PNC, stillbirths and deaths, a small set of vaccines, outpatient and inpatient visits
Reporting Rate services | ANC, Institutional Delivery, Vaccination | Adds outpatient visits
Consistency checks | ANC1 and Penta1, Penta1 and Penta3, OPV1 and OPV3, IPV1 and IPV2, plus a custom pair | ANC1 and Penta1, Penta1 and Penta3, plus a custom pair
Adjustment factors | ANC, Delivery and Vaccines K-Factors | Adds an OPD K-Factor
Denominator | One vaccination denominator | A maternal and a vaccination denominator
Coverage targets | Vaccine (BCG, Penta3, Measles 1) and Dropout | ANC4, institutional live births and vaccine
Survey inputs in the wizard | Vaccine coverage values, ANC1 and institutional delivery | Adds ANC4, C-section, low birth weight and UN mortality estimates
Extra pages | None | Bayesian analysis, continuum of care, family planning, mortality, service utilization, MCH curative index, health system performance, private sector
Saved copy | name_vaccine.rds | A saved copy for its own indicator group

A dataset saved by one app cannot be opened in the other. Opening an RMNCAH .rds in Vaxx is refused with a message that the dataset was built for a different indicator group.

sections.heading: Navigating the app
sections.text:
The left navigation has five sections. Pages under Denominators, Analysis and Output become available once the data has been adjusted.

Exports, reports and AI

Every page has a header with the page title and a Get Help button that opens the matching help chapter. Pages tied to a standard report also show a Generate Report button. The header also holds the language switch (English, French, Portuguese).

sections.heading: Recommended order
sections.text:
- Load the data and finish the wizard.
- Review the five data quality pages, then decide whether to remove years.
- Adjust the data. This unlocks the remaining pages.
- Compare denominators and choose one.
- Read national coverage, inequality, equity and targets, then the sub-national pages.
- Build a report (see Reports).

Methods behind each step are described in the framework chapters: data quality, adjustment, denominators, coverage, equity and sub-national analysis. Indicator definitions are in Indicator definitions.

sections.heading: Reports
sections.text:
The Reports page in the Output section builds reports from the loaded dataset. There are two kinds:

Kind | What it is | Files you can download
Document | Pages of text, charts and tables, with an optional cover page and contents | Word (

.docx

) or PDF
Slide deck | Slides with text boxes, charts, tables and pictures | PowerPoint (

.pptx

) or PDF

Charts and tables are drawn from the data every time you preview or download, so a report always reflects the current state of your analysis (years removed, adjustment, denominator). Every report you create is saved in the dataset and listed under Your reports. For downloading single charts and tables, datasets and the AI assistant, see Exports, reports and AI.

Reports are stored inside the dataset file. Creating or editing a report rewrites the saved dataset (the .rds cache), and the report list travels with it. Keep a copy of the dataset before you experiment, and share the dataset if you want a colleague to open your reports.

The page subtitle in the app still says "Word and PDF reports". The code also builds slide decks, and the one-pager is a PowerPoint deck.

sections.heading: Standard reports in the Vaxx App
sections.text:
A standard report is the Countdown report of one analysis section, rebuilt as editable blocks. It opens as your own copy: change or delete anything. Text blocks written as questions (headed Notes or Interpretations) are prompts for the analyst; replace them with the interpretation agreed at your review meeting.

Standard report | Kind | What it contains | Page with a

Generate Report

button
Data quality | Document | Data quality summary table, district reporting rates, consistency of ANC1/Penta1, Penta1/Penta3 and OPV1/OPV3, with questions on score, completeness and outliers | Overall Data Quality Score
Data adjustment | Document | Background, then reported BCG doses and Penta1 doses before and after adjustment for incomplete reporting and outliers, with a prompt to describe the effect in the latest year | Data Adjustment Changes
Denominator selection | Document | DHIS2 and UN projections of population, live births and under 1, then coverage of Penta3 and Measles 1 under each denominator, national and by region | Denominator Selection
National inequality | Document | For Penta3 and Measles 1: coverage by region over time, map, equity by wealth and education; then coverage by district | Equity Assessment
Synthesis chartbook | Document, chartbook page (13.9 x 22 in) | Data quality (numerators and denominators), national coverage of ANC1, institutional delivery, Penta3 and Measles 1, districts reaching the vaccine and dropout targets, and equity and geographical inequality, with interpretation questions and a cover for the country team | Reports page only
Sub-national one-pager | Slide deck, one 16:9 slide | One region: Penta3 and institutional live births against other regions and over time, the data quality score table, and population and coverage by district (ANC1, institutional births, Penta1, Penta3, MCV1, MCV3) with the region's totals | Reports page only

The Vaxx App has no standard reports for mortality, service utilization, health system or private sector, and none for national coverage on its own: those belong to the RMNCAH App. National coverage is inside the synthesis chartbook, and you can build a coverage report from blocks (see below).

The synthesis chartbook is the complete analysis in one document for the review meeting. The one-pager gives each region its own statistical profile.

sections.heading: Finish the prerequisites
sections.text: Reports stays locked until you have loaded a dataset and run Data Adjustment (see Data preparation). Choose the denominator on Denominator Selection first: the coverage charts use it.

sections.heading: Open it
sections.text: Click Reports under Output, or click Reports in the top header. A Generate Report button in a page header also opens the page and starts the matching standard report.

sections.heading: Choose a report
sections.text: Under Standard reports (documents) or Standard slide decks, click a card. Each card shows how many charts and tables it holds. You can also start from New document or New slide deck (Start blank).

sections.heading: Name it and choose its language
sections.text: A dialog asks for the report name, the Report language (English, French or Portuguese) and confirms with Create report. The report language is independent of the app language: the standard text is written in it, and the charts, tables and dates are always drawn in it. You can change it later on the Layout tab; charts and tables are redrawn, but text you wrote yourself is not translated.

sections.heading: Wait for the charts
sections.text: The editor opens at once. Each chart shows Drawing from the dataset and appears one by one. A chart that cannot be drawn shows Could not be drawn with this dataset with the reason.

sections.heading: Set the region, if the report has one
sections.text: For the one-pager (and any chart drawn for one region), pick the region on the Layout tab, under Report, in Region of this report. The first region in alphabetical order is chosen for you. Leave it empty for a national report. To produce a one-pager for every region, duplicate the report from the list and change the region.

sections.heading: Edit, then check
sections.text: Replace the prompts, delete what you do not need, then open Print layout to see the final pages (see below).

sections.heading: Download
sections.text: Choose Download, pick the format and wait for the progress bar (Drawing charts from the dataset, then Writing the Word file, Printing the PDF or Writing the PowerPoint file). The file downloads by itself; Download again is offered if it does not.

sections.heading: The document editor
sections.text:
- Blocks panel (left). The Blocks tab lists every chart and table kind that exists for the Vaxx indicators, grouped by analysis area (data quality, adjustment, denominators, national, sub-national, region profile), with a search box (Search charts, tables, text). For example Coverage trend: DHIS2 and survey, Districts reaching the target, Coverage map, Equity (from surveys) and Coverage indicators by year (DHIS2), which has a zero-dose and dropout variant for Vaxx datasets. Text and layout holds Heading, Sub-heading, Paragraph, Notes box and Page break. Drag a block onto a page, or press + to add it after the selected block. The Outline tab lists the report's structure.
- Chart and table settings. Select a block to set what it shows: Indicator, Level (National, Region or District), a variant, Year, Region, Width (Full width, Half or Third), a title and Show caption and source. Customize this chart changes text, fonts and colours for this chart in this report only. Charts you customised in the app with Apply to: Report keep that styling.
- Order and removal. Drag a block by its handle, or use Move up, Move down, Duplicate and Delete. Undo and Redo (Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y) cover edits. Changes save automatically (Saved in the dataset).
- Text. Type directly. Enter starts a paragraph, Shift+Enter a new line. Insert Fields such as {country}, {region}, {first_year}, {latest_year}, {chart_indicator} or coverage values like {penta3_latest}; they are filled in from the data and follow the report language.
- Design. The Design tab holds themes (Countdown, Ministry of Health, Minimal, Formal), colours, fonts, the Cover page (title, subtitle, logos, country flag, editors, date, reference) and Contents. Layout sets page size (A4, Letter, chartbook, poster), orientation, margins, page numbers, header and footer. Browse for Themes builds a theme from a PowerPoint or Word file (.potx, .pptx, .dotx, .docx); downloads are then written from that file.
- Views. Edit, Read mode, Print layout (the exact final pages), Focus and zoom.
- Slide decks use a slide editor with layouts, a slide sorter, speaker notes and text boxes; charts and tables are placed on slides in the same way.

sections.heading: Prerequisites that change report content
sections.text:
- Removed years and adjustment decide the numbers in every coverage and adjustment chart.
- The denominator chosen on Denominator Selection is used by the coverage charts. Without it, the coverage-by-denominator trend chart says Choose the denominators first.
- Surveys. Equity charts and facility-versus-survey comparisons need the survey files you loaded in the wizard.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.text:
Symptom | Likely cause and fix
Could not be drawn with this dataset

sections.heading: Tips for stakeholders
sections.text:
- Settle data quality, adjustment and the denominator before you generate the synthesis, and state them in a text block on the first page.
- Answer every interpretation prompt or delete it. Leaving prompts in is the most common reason a chartbook looks unfinished.
- Fill in the cover: title, editors, date and logos of the partners.
- Produce the report in the language of the audience, and use Print layout before you send a PDF.
- Duplicate the one-pager for each region and share the PowerPoint files with the regional teams or immunization managers.
- Link findings to actions: see Dissemination, decisions and action.

sections.heading: What this page does not cover
sections.text: Page notes added with the Notes button are not part of the report builder as far as the source shows. Where DataSuite saves downloaded files depends on your browser or desktop settings, which the report code does not control.

sections.heading: Sub-national analysis
sections.text:
The Sub-National Analysis section repeats the national analysis for regions (Admin 1) and districts (Admin 2). It has three pages: Sub-National Coverage, Sub-National Inequality and Coverage Target. Averages at national level often hide weak regions and districts, so this is where programme action is usually targeted. Methods: sub-national analysis.

These pages need adjusted data and use the vaccination denominator chosen in Denominators. Their indicator tabs and the Custom Check tab work as described in Coverage, equity and targets.

sections.heading: Sub-National Coverage
sections.text: Compares DHIS2 and survey estimates of coverage in each region.

sections.heading: Set the geography
sections.text: Use Admin Level (Admin 1 or Admin 2) and the region selector. Choose Admin 1 with no region to see regions, or pick a region to see its districts. At Admin 2 the selector can also pick a district.

sections.heading: Pick an indicator
sections.text: Choose a tab, or Custom Check for any Vaxx indicator, including dropout, zero-dose and under-vaccinated.

sections.heading: Read the chart
sections.text:
The chart is titled "... Coverage Estimates" for the selected area and shows the DHIS2 estimate, with the WUENIC and survey estimates where they exist for that geography. The caption gives the denominator.

Sub-national coverage

Survey and WUENIC estimates appear only where they exist for the selected geography, so some charts show DHIS2 alone.

sections.heading: Sub-National Inequality
sections.text:
Shows how coverage differs between units inside one geography.

- Filters: Admin Level and region. Each chart plots the coverage of every sub-national unit by year (legend "Coverage at subnational unit") against the coverage of the selected region or the country (legend "National Coverage", or the region name followed by "Coverage").
- The subtitle says which units are shown: "Subnational unit: admin 1 level", "district level" or the region name.
- Tabs and the Custom Check tab work as on the national page.

Use it to find districts that sit far below their region, and to see whether the gap narrows over time. A district that is always low is different from one that is low only in a bad year: the second case may be a data problem.

sections.heading: Coverage Target
sections.text:
The share of districts in a region meeting the global targets.

- Choose the region (this page has no admin level filter: the unit is always the district).
- Read the two tabs. Vaccine covers BCG, Pentavalent 3 and Measles 1 (coverage at least 80 percent at district level). Dropout covers Penta 1 to Penta 3 and Penta 3 to Measles 1 (dropout below 10 percent).
- The chart title, "Percentage of districts in (region name) meeting the ... target", shows the threshold used. Bars are percentages by year and indicator.
- The table lists the districts meeting the target for the indicator and year you select. Download it as Excel with the table's download button.

sections.heading: Interpretation and pitfalls
sections.text:
District denominators are the least reliable. A district with coverage over 100 percent, or one that flips between years, is more likely to have a population or reporting problem than a real change. Cross-check it in Data quality.

- Small districts give noisy percentages. Read several years, not one.
- Do not compare Admin 1 and Admin 2 charts directly: units differ in size and reliability.
- Changing the admin level resets the region selection.

Next: Exports, reports and AI.

sections.heading: Workflow overview
sections.text:
The CD2030 DataSuite implements an end-to-end analytical workflow that transforms raw health facility data into credible, actionable coverage estimates.
The workflow follows a logical sequence: assess data quality, correct for incompleteness and errors, select evidence-based denominators, calculate coverage, and examine inequality patterns at national and geographic levels.

Countdown analysis workflow

This structured approach addresses a universal challenge in RMNCAH monitoring: facility data are abundant but often unreliable, while surveys provide gold-standard coverage estimates but are infrequent and expensive.
The CD2030 DataSuite bridges this gap by systematically vetting facility data, calibrating them against survey benchmarks, and producing continuous trend lines with quantified uncertainty.
The result is confidence that your coverage numbers reflect reality rather than data artifacts.

sections.heading: Analysis setup
sections.text: This page describes the steps required to set up the analysis workbench.

sections.heading: Create a working folder
sections.text:
The first step in the analysis workflow is to prepare a dedicated working folder. This folder is where you keep the input files for the app, and where the system creates the derived data file used for faster future loads.

- Choose a clear directory name that you can easily remember and reference, preferably in your local environment.
- Place the raw upload (Excel) files in that folder before starting the app.
- Keep any related documentation, data or country-specific files together so the working folder is self-contained.

sections.heading: Uploading HMIS data
sections.text:
For the initial upload, use the Excel workbook generated from HMIS/DHIS2 exports. For subsequent uploads, use the cached .RDS file, which is automatically generated and stored in the working folder when the Excel file is uploaded.

The app accepts common tabular data formats for the DHIS2 upload:

- Excel workbook: .xlsx or .xls
- Comma-separated values: .csv

See the DHIS2 data indicator definitions.

sections.heading: Automatic RDS creation
sections.text:
- When you load an Excel file for the first time, the app automatically converts and saves a companion .rds file in the same working folder.
- On subsequent loads, the app checks for the existing .rds file and uses it to speed up data reloads.

This means the first load may take slightly longer while the Excel file is read and transformed. After that, the app opens the saved .rds file much faster.

sections.heading: Embedded datasets
sections.text:
In addition to the uploaded DHIS2 dataset, the app includes internal reference datasets that are linked to the country whose data was uploaded.

These embedded datasets are:

- UN estimates
- Survey data
- WUENIC estimates
- UN mortality data
- Family Planning Estimation Tool (FPET) data

Because these datasets are named according to the country whose DHIS2 data is loaded, the app can automatically match the uploaded file to the correct reference set.

Best practice

- Use one working folder per country or DHIS2 export batch.
- Keep the original Excel source file and the generated .rds file together.
- Do not rename the .rds file manually; the app manages that file automatically.

sections.heading: National parameters for denominator calculation
sections.text:
- These parameters are used to support selection of denominators for service coverage analysis within the RMNCAH analytical framework.
- They are typically derived from the most recent national survey (e.g., DHS, MICS) and are applied uniformly across subnational units.

Tip

The default values are extracted from the available country survey data. Users can update these values if they have more recent, validated values.

Analysis parameters

Parameter | Definition
ANC1 Survey (%) | Percentage of women aged 15–49 with a live birth who received at least one antenatal care (ANC) visit during their last pregnancy. (Example: If 940 out of 1,000 women had at least one ANC visit, the ANC1 coverage is 94%.)
ANC4 | Percentage of women aged 15–49 with a live birth who received four or more antenatal care visits during their last pregnancy. (Example: If 680 out of 1,000 women had ≥4 ANC visits, ANC4 coverage is 68%.)
Pregnancy Loss (proportion) | Proportion of pregnancies that ended in miscarriage, abortion, or stillbirth out of all reported pregnancy outcomes. (Example: If 80 of 1,000 pregnancies ended in loss, the proportion is 0.08)
Twin Births (proportion) | Proportion of live births that are twins out of all live births. (Example: If 30 out of 1,500 live births were twins (i.e., 15 twin pairs), the proportion is 0.02)
Neonatal Mortality (proportion) | Proportion of live births that die within the first 28 days of life out of all live births. (Example: If 20 out of 1,000 live births died within the first 28 days, the proportion is 0.02)
Post Neonatal Mortality (proportion) | Proportion of live births that die between 28 days and 11 months of life out of all live births. (Example: If 15 out of 1,000 live births died between 28 days and 11 months, the proportion is 0.015)
Stillbirth Rate (proportion) | Proportion of pregnancies that ended in stillbirth out of all reported pregnancy outcomes. (Example: If 10 out of 1,000 pregnancies ended in stillbirth, the proportion is 0.01)
Institutional delivery | Percentage of live births that occurred in a health facility. (Example: If 850 out of 1,000 live births were in a health facility, the institutional delivery coverage is 85%.)
BCG Coverage (%) | Percentage of infants aged 12–23 months who received the Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) vaccine. (Example: If 950 out of 1,000 infants received the BCG vaccine, the BCG coverage is 95%.)
Penta1 Coverage (%) | Percentage of infants aged 12–23 months who received the first dose of pentavalent vaccine. (Example: If 920 out of 1,000 infants received the first dose, the Penta 1 coverage is 92%.)
Penta 3 | Percentage of infants aged 12–23 months who received the third dose of pentavalent vaccine. (Example: If 850 out of 1,000 infants received the third dose, the Penta 3 coverage is 85%.)
Measles 1 Coverage (%) | Percentage of infants aged 12–23 months who received the first dose of measles vaccine. (Example: If 900 out of 1,000 infants received the first dose, the Measles1 coverage is 90%.)
C-Section Rate (%) | Percentage of live births that were delivered by cesarean section. (Example: If 150 out of 1,000 live births were by C-section, the C-section coverage is 15%.)
Low birth weight | Percentage of live births that were low birth weight (less than 2,500 grams). (Example: If 100 out of 1,000 live births were low birth weight, the low birth weight coverage is 10%.)
Recent survey Year | The calendar year in which the survey was conducted and from which vaccine coverage estimates (e.g., BCG, Penta1/3, Measles1) are drawn. (Example: If the survey was conducted in 2022, that is the vaccine survey year).
Survey Data Start Year | The calendar year from which the survey data starts. This is used to determine the time period for which the survey data is relevant. Ideally, it is recommended to use the two most recent surveys for this analysis. (Example: If a country has survey data for 2008, 2013, 2018 and 2023; the Survey data start should be 2018 (two most recent)).
